bounds_and_cleanup.json_scanning: Both raw JSON bytes and decoded string values/keys are inspected; decoded aggregate <=2MiB and <=8000 traversal nodes. Avoids losing escaped multiline literal content.
bounds_and_cleanup.parser: Reuses unchanged GCP _tar/_descriptor and shared package strict JSON/media types. Verifies original compressed SHA256 and uncompressed rootfs diff ID before pseudonymizing every path to ordinal names; own memory-only loop requires complete TAR terminator, bounded offsets and only preflight-admitted regular files/directories. Rejects links/devices/extensions/duplicate original paths/nested archives/concatenated gzip. No extract/extractall, Docker or shell execution.
bounds_and_cleanup.time_scope: Shared120-second reader deadline and Azure cancellation/call/resource budgets cover native transfers/parsing/detectors. Existing SDK credential acquisition has its own Azure transport behavior and is not newly instrumented as a native content HTTP call.
bounds_and_cleanup.transport: Direct TLS with default certificate validation to verified fixed ARM/native ACR origins; no environment proxy/netrc/redirect library/challenge parsing. One native307 data hop only, no auth forwarded, exact native approved hosts; response body/error/signed location never cached.
bounds_and_cleanup.cleanup: Every response/connection closes in finally including denial, digest failure, unsupported redirect and parser failures. No content files, extraction directories or raw persistent response cache. Shared scanner cache uses HMAC keys and canonical redacted results; Python memory is not guaranteed cryptographic erasure.

proof_limits: All tests offline: fake independent native HTTPS responses assert method+host+route/form and block sockets/DNS/auth discovery; no live Azure RBAC/token or cloud service exercise. Native response parsing and authorization config are not proof of effective access or credential validity.

Both tools inspect supported selected observed bytes and decoded JSON strings only; detector rules do not recognize every possible secret format, encryption or encoding. No all-service, history, deployed-workload or currently-running-image coverage claim.

Multiarch indexes deterministically UNKNOWN; no implicit local platform selection. Only Linux amd64/arm64 single-platform OCI/Docker schema2, supported raw/gzip regular-file layers. zstd/foreign/nested archive/link/device/extension/duplicate or partial forms unresolved.

Only public native Azure ACR endpoints and bounded safe ASCII registry ARM/resource-group/repository names are supported. Opaque/regional/sovereign aliases, unsupported native host shapes and default wildcard Azure Storage redirects remain UNKNOWN; no arbitrary source URL is fetched.

JWT signature validation is not reimplemented: existing Azure token transport and fixed certificate-validated native TLS authority provide the credentials; conservative JWT claim checks only reject expired/foreign/overbroad shapes and do not certify user-supplied signatures.
Layers are inspected independently, including bytes removed/overwritten by later whiteouts; a finding can reflect a historical layer copy and does not assert final container filesystem exposure.
